source.citation: Elzinga D, Sternburg E, Sabbadin D, Bartsch M, Park S-Y, Vaidya A, Mosquna A, Kaundal A, Wendeborn S, Lachia M, Karginov FV, Cutler SR. Defining and Exploiting Hypersensitivity Hotspots to Facilitate Abscisic Acid Agonist Optimization. ACS Chem Biol. 2019 Mar 15;14(3):332-336.
source.pdf: data/papers/Defining and Exploiting Hypersensitivity Hotspots to Facilitate/cb8b00955.pdf
source.assay: Y2H staining, limit of detection for ABA response
source.caveat: 0.25 uM is the LOWEST concentration tested, so every 0.25 entry is a FLOOR, not a measurement. Jannis: F61, V81 and A160 look strongest and would likely score below 0.25 if lower concentrations had been used.

itc.note: the only direct affinity measurement; >10x tighter than WT

si_table_s2.what: Calculated ABA EC50 (uM) for single and combined PYR1 mutants, receptor-PP2C assay. Page 15 of cb8b00955_si_001.pdf.

interpretation.positive_only: These are hypersensitive mutations FOUND. A substitution absent from this table is UNTESTED, not worse. Use for RECALL only, never precision.
interpretation.wt_is_not_optimal: WT PYR1 is a functional compromise, not an ABA affinity optimum. Any scorer, filter or library rule must ALLOW the WT identity, never assert it is the best one.
interpretation.all_five_verified: Identities asserted against data/3QN1_complex_auth_aba.pdb chain A: 61 IS F, 81 IS V, 110 IS I, 141 IS E, 160 IS A. All five lie within 5.4 A of ABA (3.51, 5.39, 3.51, 3.99, 4.57).
interpretation.all_five_in_lining_set: All five are already in the 23-position LINING list used by 211_position_scan.py.
interpretation.all_five_in_stage3_motif: All five fall inside the 10ext3 extended motif (A58-65, A79-94, A108-122, A141-168) -- the Stage 3 scaffold is being built around exactly the residues that tune ABA affinity.

super_additive.note: BOTH are A160 x F61 and BOTH land at ~2.9x above the product, so the A160-F61 coupling is worth ~3x and is robust to which substitution is used.

sign_epistasis.F61M: alone 0.29x (EC50 2.98 vs WT 0.864, i.e. 3.4x WORSE), but A160V+F61M is 7.6x BETTER than WT. An individually deleterious substitution is beneficial in the right background -- an additive objective cannot represent this.

A160V+F61L+I110C+V81I.note: 1.26x WORSE than A160V alone (0.124 vs 0.0982). Stacking hypersensitive mutations DEGRADES; it does not saturate.

assay_disagreement.what: 3 of 8 Y2H-hypersensitive mutants do not show improved in vitro EC50: F61M 0.29x, I110S 0.75x, I110C 0.99x.
assay_disagreement.DO_NOT_CONCLUDE: That Y2H 'overstates' or is wrong. THE TWO ASSAYS MEASURE DIFFERENT QUANTITIES and neither is ground truth for the other.
why: Y2H reports CELLULAR ternary-complex formation: compound entry into yeast, expression, and PYR1-HAB1 association. SI Table S2 reports IN VITRO receptor-PP2C EC50 on purified protein. A mutant can genuinely be better in one and not the other.
The Y2H is CENSORED. Only 0/0.25/0.5/1/5 uM were tested, so every 0.25 entry is a FLOOR, not a measurement -- the true LOD may be far lower. A censored floor cannot 'overstate'.
The hypersensitivity call was staining intensity at 1 uM judged against a WT control in 2 experiments (Figure S1 caption). That is an ordinal call, not an affinity, and it does not convert to one.
Jannis: 'The yeast two hybrid works on a different calculation and was not measured to its limits for all substitutions.'
assay_disagreement.how_to_use: Use EC50 as the primary benchmark for AFFINITY because it is quantitative and continuous. Use Y2H for CELLULAR responsiveness. Do NOT treat a Y2H-only entry as refuted by the absence of an EC50 improvement, and do NOT drop F61M/I110C/I110S from the hypersensitive set -- they are hypersensitive in the assay that measured them.

ec50_confirmed._note: These 5 are the substitutions with a quantitative in vitro EC50 improvement. They are a CLEANER AFFINITY subset, not a corrected version of the Y2H set.
